title: The poor ox belongs to no one
odia:
ଗାଈ ସହଦେବଙ୍କର
ଷଣ୍ଢ ମହାଦେବଙ୍କର
ବଳଦ ବାପୁଡା କହାରି ନୁହେଁ।
literal_meaning: The cow belongs to Sahadeva; the bull belongs to Mahadeva; the poor ox belongs to no one.
meaning_odia: ଗାଈ ପାଇଁ ସହଦେବଙ୍କ ନାମ, ଷଣ୍ଢ ପାଇଁ ମହାଦେବଙ୍କ ନାମ ଅଛି; ବଳଦ ବାପୁଡାର କେହି ନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କର ଆପଣା ଲୋକ ବା ସାହାରା ଥିବା ବେଳେ ଜଣେ ଏକା ଓ ଅବହେଳିତ ରହିଯିବାର କ୍ଷୋଭ ଓ କରୁଣା ଏଠାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ।
explanation: The first two lines give the cow and bull a named affiliation. The third breaks the pattern: the ox has nobody. Our editorial reading hears sympathy for someone left without support while others have a person to whom they belong. The affectionate pity in “poor ox” gives the ending its emotional weight.
usage_example: Original imagined example: In a group where most people can turn to a supporter, one member feels overlooked. A reader uses the saying’s final line to describe that feeling of having nobody in their corner.
cultural_context: The repeated possessive endings after Sahadeva and Mahadeva establish an expectation of belonging. The ox’s line replaces a name with “no one.” Cow, bull and ox stay distinct in the translation so that the three-part comparison remains visible.

odia_summary: ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କର ସାହାରା ଥିବା ବେଳେ ଜଣେ କାହାରି ନହୋଇ ରହିଯିବା।
english_summary: Sympathy for the one left without anyone to claim or support them.
